comments.author: Brandon T.
comments.text: Channel 9 just put up 3,000 ACRES and KESTREL SPRINGS UNDER EVACUATION on the screen. Their map has the fire all the way to the Stonebridge area. Mill Creek Bridge is jammed, which way do we go??

comments.author: Shelly R.
comments.text: The school district told the parents in the pickup line it's 1,500 acres. So which is it?? I called 911 and they put me on hold.

comments.author: Gary W.
comments.text: I'm on Kestrel Springs Road by the mailboxes and I don't see flames, just a lot of smoke to the west. Where was this picture taken? It's pitch dark in that photo and it's 4 in the afternoon.

instructorNote: This is a misinformation inject about conflicting acreage and zone status. The attached photo is from a 2020 fire in another state, and the Channel 9 chyron took its perimeter from the co-op's outage map. After showing the post, read the co-op care lead's text to the PIO: "Callers say the school district told them it's 1,500 acres. Which number do we give out?" Watch whether, within 30 minutes, the PIO logs the rumor, aligns the Sheriff, DFPC, the co-op, the schools and the hospital, then sends a WEA and a SawmillAlert under EOP 6 and SENTCS 7 that quote only the IC's acreage with its time (for example, 1,100 acres and 0 percent at 15:20) and name each zone's status exactly as the board shows it, without calling any zone "safe".

citations.documentTitle: SOP-WF-01: Evacuation Notification, Traffic Control and Sheltering
citations.quote: The county never repeats a fire agency perimeter or acreage as its own; it quotes the Incident Commander and the time. The PIO keeps a rumor log; examples: "Kestrel Springs is burning" (not confirmed)

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Night-time phone snapshot of a two-story wood-frame suburban house fully engulfed in flames, fire roaring from the upper windows and through the collapsing roofline, thick dark smoke rising into a pitch-black sky. Bright orange glow lights up bare leafless deciduous trees in the front yard and a wet paved suburban curb and sidewalk in the foreground. Flat lawn and level street, with neighbouring houses in shadow at the edges. Shot handheld from across the street, slight tilt, motion blur and grainy low-light noise, blown-out highlights in the fire, deep black shadows. A chaotic, frightening amateur image. Setting: on a hillside road: a fire engine with lights on, hose lines, a smoke column above a ridge, dry grass and oak brush, a utility pole with a line crew truck
